run_metadata.coverage_summary: DEGRADED RUN (network egress restricted). All direct WebFetch/curl egress was blocked this session: every external HTTPS host returned a proxy 403 (CONNECT tunnel failed) / EGRESS_BLOCKED, including example.com, so this was a blanket egress denial, not a site outage. Consequently NO tender detail page or specification document could be opened, and no deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, values or contacts could be extracted or verified from any notice. The only working external tool was WebSearch (an index that returns titles, URLs and short snippets). Discovery was therefore limited to headline-level opportunities that were corroborated across search snippets pointing to a buyer-originated source; several candidate opportunities surfaced by a single snippet were EXCLUDED as insufficiently corroborated. Tier 1 (AusTender + state portals), Tier 2 (councils/GBEs/universities/health) and Tier 3 (SAP Ariba Discovery + major-buyer portals) were probed via WebSearch only, not read directly. Nothing was fabricated: all captured tenders are marked headline-level and pending detail, and every closing date/value shown is from a search snippet and flagged for re-verification.
gaps: NETWORK EGRESS BLOCK (primary cause of degraded run): every WebFetch call and every Bash curl to an external host was denied by the session egress proxy (proxy returned HTTP 403 on CONNECT / tool returned EGRESS_BLOCKED). Confirmed blocked this run: www.tenders.gov.au, www.tenders.nsw.gov.au, and example.com (a control host), indicating a blanket outbound-HTTPS denial for this session rather than a per-site restriction. Per environment policy, org egress denials were reported, not retried or routed around. Recommend allowlisting Australian tender domains (and general web egress) for this scheduled routine so detail extraction can resume.

Tier 1 core portals (AusTender, buy.nsw/tenders.nsw, Buying for Victoria, QTenders/supply.qld, Tenders WA, Tenders SA, Tenders Tasmania, NT QTOL, ACT Tenders) could not be queried or paginated directly; only incidental WebSearch snippets were available. No exhaustive Tier 1 sweep was possible.

Tier 2 (local councils via VendorPanel, GBEs such as Sydney/Melbourne/SA Water, WaterNSW, universities, health districts) could not be crawled or read; where water utilities were probed, Melbourne Water advertises via Buying for Victoria and Sydney Water via NSW eTendering + SAP Ariba (registration) — recorded as sources, no current opportunity verified.

Tier 3 MANDATORY corporate channel: SAP Ariba Discovery / SAP Business Network Discovery and major-buyer portals (BHP via GCMS+Ariba+interestedsupplier.bhp.com) were confirmed to exist and to be registration-gated, but could NOT be authenticated or read via WebFetch, so no publicly-visible current corporate opportunity could be captured or verified. Corporate portals are recorded in discovered_sources (access_method=portal-registration). No corporate tenders fabricated. Invitation-only management-consultancy RFPs remain out of scope.

Detail/deliverables extraction was impossible for every opportunity this run because tender detail pages and documents were unreachable (egress block). All five captured tenders are headline-level only and are counted in entries_pending_detail; deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, values, closing times and contacts are left null/empty rather than inferred.

EXCLUDED as under-corroborated (surfaced by a single WebSearch snippet and not confirmable against a buyer-originated notice this run, so not captured to avoid fabrication): a WA Health 'CIIP' infrastructure upgrade in the Great Southern region reportedly closing 25-Sep-2026 (Tenders WA); a National Parks & Wildlife Service road-cutting slope stabilisation reportedly closing 21-Sep-2026 (NSW eTendering); and a drainage/pavement/median/signage works item at Parker & Stafford St, Penrith which appeared to be a SELECT (invitation-only) tender and is therefore out of scope.

Closing dates/times and any scope wording shown on the captured tenders come from WebSearch snippets, not from the notices themselves, and must be re-verified against the buyer portal on a run with fetch access. CSIROEOI2026001 (Parkes Observatory cafe EOI) appeared in both 'current' and 'closed' AusTender views in the index, so its status is uncertain and flagged.
recommended_seed_additions: University of Adelaide E-Tendering (TenderLink) — https://portal.tenderlink.com/adelaideuni/alltenders/ (buyer-originated SA university e-tendering portal; newly observed this run).
Adelaide Primary Health Network Ltd E-Tendering (TenderLink) — https://portal.tenderlink.com/adelaidephn (buyer-originated PHN/health-NFP e-tendering portal; newly observed this run).
Reaffirm allowlisting/egress for AusTender and the state portals so machine-readable detail extraction (ATM detail pages, ATM feed) can resume.
